subject: science
intro: I'm Mr. Patel. Let's plan an engineering-focused 6th grade lesson on thermal energy transfer.

beats.narration: An engineering challenge title tells students they'll be building something.
This standard asks students to design a device that minimizes or maximizes thermal energy transfer.
Design, test, improve is the engineering cycle; explaining ties it back to the science.
beats.text: Students will be able to design, test, and improve a device that minimizes thermal energy transfer, explaining how it reduces conduction, convection, and radiation.

beats.narration: This common misconception sets up the idea of conduction.
beats.text: "Why does a metal bench feel colder than a wooden one on the same day?" Students discuss.

beats.narration: Three quick demos, one for each concept.
beats.text: Model the three types of heat transfer with quick demos: a metal spoon in hot water (conduction), food coloring in warm water (convection), and a lamp on skin (radiation).

beats.narration: The materials limit forces tradeoffs, which is what real engineering is about.
beats.text: Challenge: with limited materials (foil, felt, bubble wrap, cardboard), groups design a container to keep an ice cube from melting for 30 minutes. Test, measure the meltwater, and redesign.

beats.narration: This connects their design back to the science concept.
beats.text: Which material worked best in your design? Explain using at least one type of heat transfer.

outro: Misconception, demos, design challenge. Now you plan one.
